title: Leads that break the CRM
scenario: A sales team extracts leads from inbound emails into its CRM: name, email, company, phone and plan. Today the prompt says 'Return JSON with these fields' and the code runs JSON.parse on the reply. About 3% of replies fail to parse. Some leads have phone numbers that appear nowhere in the email. The dashboard counts 'Enterprise', 'enterprise' and 'Enterprise Plan' as three different plans. You review a sample (exhibit).
exhibit:
PROMPT
Extract the lead from this email. Return JSON with name, email,
company, phone, plan.

REPLY 1 (parse error)
Sure! Here is the JSON:
{"name": "Ana Silva", "email": "ana@example.com", ...}

REPLY 2 (email has no phone number)
{"name": "Tom Berg", "email": "tom@example.com",
 "company": "Nordic Freight", "phone": "+46 555 0199",
 "plan": "Enterprise Plan"}

questions.prompt: What is the best fix for the parse errors?

options.text: Use the vendor's structured outputs feature with a JSON Schema for the lead.
options.explanation: Right. Structured outputs constrain the reply to the schema: Claude's output_config.format or OpenAI's text.format with strict: true.

options.text: Turn on JSON mode, which guarantees the fields you need.
options.explanation: JSON mode gives valid JSON but does not guarantee any specific schema. The OpenAI docs recommend Structured Outputs over JSON mode when possible.

options.text: Retry each failed call in a loop until JSON.parse succeeds, with no limit on attempts.
options.explanation: Unlimited retries waste money and hide the cause. Structured outputs remove this class of error.

options.text: Strip everything before the first brace with a regular expression.
options.explanation: A patch for one symptom. It does not fix missing fields or wrong types.

questions.prompt: How should the schema and prompt handle the phone number?

options.text: Keep phone as a required string, so that every single lead has a phone number.
options.explanation: That is the bug. A required string forces the model to fill the field, even when the email has no number.

options.text: Allow string or null, say 'null if no phone given', and check it in code.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI emulates optional fields with a union with null and advises saying what to return when the input does not fit. The Gemini docs say to validate values.

options.text: Add more examples in the prompt that all include a phone number.
options.explanation: Examples that always have a phone teach the model that a phone is always there. That makes invention more likely.

options.text: Remove the phone field from the CRM.
options.explanation: The business needs phone numbers when they exist. Fix the schema, not the product.

questions.prompt: How should the plan field be designed?

options.text: A free-text string, cleaned up by the sales team each month.
options.explanation: Free text is how the three spellings appeared. Manual cleanup does not scale.

options.text: Two fields, plan and plan_name, so the model can choose either.
options.explanation: Two overlapping fields create more variants, not fewer.

options.text: An enum (starter, team, enterprise), compared case-insensitively in code.
options.explanation: Right. Enums fix the set of values. Claude may vary capitalization, so its docs say to compare enum values case-insensitively.

options.text: An enum, and trust the exact casing, because structured outputs guarantee it.
options.explanation: The Claude docs say structured outputs don't guarantee the capitalization of enum values.

questions.prompt: After the switch, a few replies still don't match the schema. What should the code check first?

options.text: Whether the model needs a larger context window for these requests.
options.explanation: The context window is not the usual reason for a schema mismatch. Check the stop reason first.

options.text: Whether the JSON Schema has a syntax error.
options.explanation: A bad schema causes an API error on every call, not a few mismatched replies.

options.text: Whether to switch back to plain prompting.
options.explanation: Plain prompting has no enforcement at all. The known edge cases can be detected and handled.

options.text: The stop reason: a refusal, or a reply cut off by the token limit.
options.explanation: Right. Both vendors list refusals and hitting the max tokens limit as cases where output may not match the schema.
